Under the U.S. Constitution, the President has the power to approve legislation by signing a bill and to veto it after it passes both houses of Congress [d1][d7][d8]. Congress, however, can override a presidential veto by a two-thirds vote in both the House and the Senate [d5][d7][d8]. If you mean a state constitution instead, the answer can differ; for example, the Virginia Constitution gives that role to the Governor, with override power in the state legislature [d9].
